title_en: China Cinda Asset Management Corporation Xi'an Office v. Hainan Huashan Real Estate Development Corporation and China Construction Bank Corporation Xi'an Qujiang Branch — dispute over loan contract
ruling_gist_en: When parties enter into a civil contract, they have complex motives, purposes, and functions. In addition to establishing specific transactional relationships, contracts may also serve normative and guiding functions, i.e., the parties use the contract to regulate and guide future rights and obligations. Contracts may also have confirmatory and evaluative functions, i.e., the parties use the contract to confirm, supplement, improve, and evaluate the nature, purpose, and effect of their past civil legal acts.

full_text_en:
China Cinda Asset Management Corporation Xi'an Office v. Hainan Huashan Real Estate Development Corporation and China Construction Bank Corporation Xi'an Qujiang Sub-branch — dispute over loan contract

[Ruling Summary]

When parties enter into civil contracts, they may have complex motives, purposes, and functions. In addition to establishing specific transactional relationships, contracts can also serve normative and guiding functions, i.e., the parties may use the contract to regulate and guide future rights and obligations. Contracts may also serve confirmation and evaluation functions, i.e., the parties may use the contract to confirm, supplement, improve, and evaluate the nature, purpose, and function of their previous civil legal acts.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court

(2008) Min Er Zhong Zi No. 118

Appellant (Plaintiff at First Instance): China Cinda Asset Management Corporation Xi'an Office. Domicile: No. 15 South Street, Xi'an City, Shaanxi Province.

Responsible Person: Li Yuejin, Director of the Office.

Agent ad litem: Xu Meng, lawyer of Beijing V&T Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Wen Chengwei, lawyer of Beijing V&T Law Firm.

Appellee (Defendant at First Instance): Hainan Huashan Real Estate Development Corporation. Domicile: Block A, No. 12 Huashan Villa Zone, Longkun North Road, Haikou City, Hainan Province.

Legal Representative: Gao Wenxuan, General Manager of the Corporation.

Agent ad litem: Nie Xijing, Deputy General Manager of the Corporation.

Agent ad litem: Liu Xi, lawyer of Hainan Zetian Law Firm.

Third Party at First Instance: China Construction Bank Corporation Xi'an Qujiang Sub-branch. Domicile: No. 12 Yanta South Road, Xi'an City, Shaanxi Province.

Responsible Person: Feng Tao, President of the Sub-branch.

Agent ad litem: Li Jinzheng, staff member of the Sub-branch.

The appellant, China Cinda Asset Management Corporation Xi'an Office (hereinafter referred to as Cinda Xi'an Office), appealed to this Court against the civil judgment (2006) Qiong Min Yi Chu (Chong) Zi No. 1 rendered by the Hainan High People's Court in the case of dispute over loan contract with the appellee, Hainan Huashan Real Estate Development Corporation (hereinafter referred to as Huashan Corporation), and the third party at first instance, China Construction Bank Corporation Xi'an Qujiang Sub-branch (hereinafter referred to as CCB Qujiang Sub-branch). This Court formed a collegial panel in accordance with the law, with Judge Qian Xiaochen serving as the presiding judge, and acting judges Liu Min and Yang Zhengyu participating in the trial. The clerk Yuan Hongxia recorded the proceedings. The trial of this case has now been concluded.

On October 8, 2003, Cinda Xi'an Office filed a lawsuit with the Shaanxi High People's Court against Huashan Corporation, requesting: 1. an order that Huashan Corporation repay the loan principal of RMB 62,256,100 (with interest calculated up to June 20, 2003), plus interest up to the date of actual repayment; and 2. an order that Huashan Corporation bear all litigation costs of this case. During the trial, the Shaanxi High People's Court, upon the application of Huashan Corporation, added CCB Qujiang Sub-branch as a third party to the case. After trial, the court found that there was a cooperative development contract relationship between Huashan Corporation and CCB Qujiang Sub-branch, which had not been terminated or liquidated. It also found that the loan funds involved in this case were project funds for the performance of the cooperative development agreement. Since the place of performance of the cooperative development contract was Haikou City, Hainan Province, and the real property involved in the cooperative development contract was located in Haikou City, Hainan Province, the case was transferred to the Hainan High People's Court for trial. On February 4, 2005, the Hainan High People's Court rendered civil judgment (2004) Qiong Min Yi Chu Zi No. 2, dismissing Cinda Xi'an Office's claims. Cinda Xi'an Office appealed to this Court. On December 21, 2005, this Court rendered civil ruling (2005) Min Er Zhong Zi No. 82, ordering a retrial of the case. On April 30, 2008, the Hainan High People's Court rendered civil judgment (2006) Qiong Min Yi Chu (Chong) Zi No. 1.

Upon retrial, the Hainan High People's Court found the following facts:

On November 14, 1992, Huashan Corporation and the People's Construction Bank of China, Shaanxi Provincial Trust and Investment Corporation (hereinafter referred to as Shaanxi Construction Trust) entered into an *Economic Cooperation Contract*. The contract provided: 1. Method of cooperation: Each party invested RMB 2 million as a cooperation fund for joint project development and construction. Purpose of cooperation: To jointly invest and raise funds to select viable projects in the Hainan Special Economic Zone and other regions for development and construction, and to share the proceeds of the investment projects. Term of cooperation: From the date of signing the contract to December 31, 1997. 3. The cooperation fund was to be managed separately. Each party was to send two members, and an additional advisor was to be hired to jointly form a Cooperation Fund Management Committee, which would decide on the following matters: selecting investment projects, appointing the principal responsible person of the project headquarters, approving the project budget, deciding on the construction unit, organizing project acceptance, approving the final project accounts, determining the sales price, deciding on the method of profit distribution, and other major matters. After the Management Committee decided on a project, it would establish a project headquarters for that project, which would be responsible to the Management Committee and specifically manage the project's various tasks in accordance with the Management Committee's decisions. 5. All funds raised by the cooperation fund for the project were to have different interest rates determined according to the different sources of funds, and all interest was to be included in the project cost. 6. After the project determined by the cooperation fund was completed, all income was to be distributed in the following order: unpaid project amounts, taxes, principal and interest of bank loans, and other principal and interest of the project. The net income was to be used to withdraw 3% as a special project fund, and the remaining income was to be distributed between the parties in the proportion of 60% for Huashan Corporation and 40% for Shaanxi Construction Trust. 7. Responsibilities and obligations of the parties: Huashan Corporation was to promptly select suitable projects to recommend to the Management Committee. After a project was determined, it was to supervise and assist the project headquarters in project establishment, approval, design, bidding, and other matters. Shaanxi Construction Trust was to actively raise funds required for the project's construction, ensure the project's use of funds, provide RMB 50 million in loans to the cooperative project at an annual interest rate of 15%, and satisfy the cooperative project's funding needs to the extent possible. 9. This contract was to become effective and have legal force upon being signed and sealed by the legal representatives of both parties. On January 9 and 19, 1993, the parties respectively signed the *Cooperative Construction of "Huashan New Village" Contract* and the *Cooperative Construction of "Shishan Resort" Contract*. Both contracts were standard form contracts, with identical provisions except for differences in project name, address, and floor area. They provided: I. With the consent of the "Cooperation Fund Management Committee," the parties agreed to cooperate in constructing the "Huashan New Village" and "Shishan Resort" projects. II. Principles of cooperation: The projects were to be jointly selected and cooperatively constructed by the parties. Construction costs were to be jointly borne by both parties. The completed houses were to be jointly owned by both parties. The parties guaranteed close cooperation. If the project was profitable, it was to be shared by both parties in accordance with the agreement. If there were risks, they were to be jointly borne by both parties. III. The Management Committee was to allocate RMB 2 million from the cooperation fund to each of the two projects. The "Huashan New Village" project required funds: from March 1993 to January 1994, five loans totaling RMB 45 million were needed. The "Shishan Resort" project, Phase I, required funds: from March 1993 to February 1994, five loans totaling RMB 18 million were needed. The above loans were expected to begin repayment in the second half of 1994. The source of repayment was the proceeds from the sale of houses in each project, which, according to analysis, could be fully repaid within six months. IV. Both parties agreed to and dispatched personnel to formally establish project headquarters for the two projects, which were to be directly under the leadership of the Management Committee. Special accounts were to be opened for the projects, and all funds were to be transferred through these special accounts. V. Responsibilities of the parties: Huashan Corporation guaranteed that the construction funds provided by Shaanxi Construction Trust for the project cooperation would be used for the specified purpose only and was responsible for supervising the project headquarters in completing the project construction. Shaanxi Construction Trust guaranteed to provide loans to Huashan Corporation in a timely manner in accordance with the loan plan in the contract. Specific loan procedures: The project headquarters, in the name of Huashan Corporation, was to prepare the necessary documents to apply for loans from Shaanxi Construction Trust, and the project headquarters was to pay the loan interest on time. VI. This contract was to become effective upon being signed and sealed by both parties. After all houses in the two projects were sold and the profit distribution was completed, this contract was to automatically terminate.

In accordance with the above cooperative contracts, Huashan Corporation and Shaanxi Construction Trust executed six *Loan Contracts* between May 1992 and November 1993: (92) No. 4, 5, 8, 10 and (93) No. 1, 12, with loan amounts of RMB 2 million, RMB 3 million, RMB 5 million, RMB 4 million, and two of RMB 10 million, totaling RMB 34 million. On December 29, 1995, the parties executed another Loan Contract No. 10 for RMB 10 million. Huashan Corporation stated that this sum was converted from interest on the aforementioned RMB 34 million (hereinafter referred to as interest-converted loan), which was acknowledged by both Cinda Xi'an Office and CCB Qujiang Sub-branch in pretrial evidence verification and at trial. In 1996, Shaanxi Construction Trust was restructured into the Second Direct Sub-branch of China Construction Bank, Shaanxi Branch (hereinafter referred to as CCB Second Sub-branch) by virtue of the Reply No. Shan Yin Fu (1996) 20 of the Shaanxi Branch of the People's Bank of China. On December 31, 1998, Huashan Corporation and CCB Second Sub-branch executed Loan Contract No. 98026, providing for a loan of RMB 44 million to repay the original loan of RMB 44 million (the original loan was used for Shishan development), thereby rolling over the original loan.

On November 5, 1999, CCB Second Sub-branch issued a *Debt Amount Verification Sheet* to Huashan Corporation, requesting verification of a loan principal of RMB 54 million and an interest balance of RMB 4,647,764.50 as of September 20 of the same year. On November 20 of the same month, Huashan Corporation confirmed on the *Debt Amount Verification Receipt* that the verification was accurate and no objections; it attached four attachments: *Economic Cooperation Contract*, *Cooperative Construction of "Huashan New Village" Contract*, *Cooperative Construction of "Shishan Resort" Contract*, and *Explanation on Debt Amount*, and handwritten a remark: "The above attachments are causally linked to the Debt Amount Verification Sheet, are inseparable in nature, and have the same legal effect." Among them, the attachment *Explanation on Debt Amount* stated: "1. The principal and interest of RMB 58.65 million listed in the verification sheet are the loan principal and interest of the cooperative project between Huashan Corporation and CCB Second Sub-branch, to be settled together by both parties upon the conclusion of the cooperative project. 2. According to the provisions of the cooperative contract signed by both parties, the parties jointly established a project headquarters. The project headquarters, in the name of Huashan Corporation, applied for loans from Shaanxi Construction Trust, and the funds were deposited into the special account of the cooperative project of both parties. Given the current situation of the cooperative project, our company believes that continuing to affix our seal on behalf of the cooperative project for future loans would be inappropriate and would cause unclear creditor-debtor relationships for this special loan, leading to unnecessary judicial disputes. 3. Because the principal and interest listed in this verification sheet are inseparable from the cooperative project of both parties, while transferring the creditor's rights in this cooperative project to Cinda Xi'an Office, your sub-branch should also transfer the main body of the cooperative project to facilitate the continued cooperative development or liquidation of the project."

On December 1, 1999, CCB Second Sub-branch, as Party A, and Cinda Xi'an Office, as Party B, executed a *Creditor's Rights Transfer Agreement*, providing that: Party A transferred to Party B the loan creditor's rights against the borrower Huashan Corporation as of September 20, 1999, including principal of RMB 54 million and accrued interest of RMB 3,224,558.50; Party B succeeded to Party A's status as creditor. Party A warranted that the transferred creditor's rights and their ancillary rights were true, lawful, and valid; that no third party would dispute the ownership of such creditor's rights; and that all legal documents delivered were true, lawful, and valid. If Party A failed to fulfill the above warranties, the creditor's rights transfer would be void. After this agreement was signed, Party A was to notify the borrower and guarantor of the transfer and be responsible for collecting the receipts. The agreement did not include the content of the cooperative contract or the cooperative project. After the agreement was signed, CCB Second Sub-branch notified Huashan Corporation. On the *Receipt of Notice of Creditor's Rights Transfer*, Huashan Corporation also attached: *Economic Cooperation Contract*, *Cooperative Construction of "Huashan New Village" Contract*, *Cooperative Construction of "Shishan Resort" Contract*, and *Explanation on Debt Amount*. Thereafter, Cinda Xi'an Office made demands for payment to Huashan Corporation.

It was further found that in 1993, Huashan Corporation, Shaanxi Construction Trust, and Hainan Province Commercial Storage and Transportation Corporation, among others, prepared to establish Hainan Huashan Industrial Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Huashan Joint Stock Company). Shaanxi Construction Trust subscribed to 11 million shares of Huashan Joint Stock Company and obtained a shareholding certificate with code 01135. On November 13, 1996, CCB Second Sub-branch issued a *Letter of Authorization* to Huashan Corporation, stating: "Our sub-branch has signed a share subscription agreement for RMB 11 million with Huashan Joint Stock Company. We hereby authorize Huashan Corporation to transfer the RMB 11 million originally subscribed by our sub-branch to Huashan Joint Stock Company as capital contribution." On April 2, 1997, Huashan Joint Stock Company commissioned Hainan Certified Public Accountants to issue a *Capital Verification Report*. Item 2 of Article 3 of the *Explanation on Capital Verification Matters* attached to the report stated: "Shaanxi Construction Trust converted its former working capital loans to Huashan Corporation into capital contributions to Huashan Joint Stock Company, with Huashan Corporation making the capital contribution on behalf of Shaanxi Construction Trust." In its *Basic Information on Hainan Huashan Industrial Co., Ltd.* dated May 30, 1997, CCB Second Sub-branch stated: "For the subscription of 11 million legal person shares, our sub-branch made no new capital injection; instead, it used land purchased with RMB 11 million out of the RMB 34 million loan for the cooperative investment and development project with Huashan Corporation as a capital contribution in kind."

In 1999, CCB Second Sub-branch was renamed to China Construction Bank Xi'an Dongdajie Sub-branch (hereinafter referred to as CCB Dongdajie Sub-branch) by virtue of Reply No. Xi Yin Fu (1999) 157 of the Xi'an Branch of the People's Bank of China. In 2007, upon approval by the Shaanxi Regulatory Bureau of the China Banking Regulatory Commission, CCB Dongdajie Sub-branch relocated from No. 15 South Street, Xi'an City, Shaanxi Province to No. 2 Yanta South Road, and was renamed to China Construction Bank Corporation Xi'an Qujiang Sub-branch, i.e., the aforementioned CCB Qujiang Sub-branch.

The Xi'an Office of China Xinda Asset Management Corporation (hereinafter "Xinda Xi'an Office"), dissatisfied with the foregoing civil judgment of the court of first instance, appealed to this Court, alleging: 1. The finding of the first-instance judgment that the loans under the Loan Contracts were related to the cooperative development is inconsistent with the facts. The three cooperation contracts were signed on November 14, 1992, January 9, 1993, and January 19, 1993, respectively. The contracts stipulated the loan purpose, loan term, loan account, loan interest rate, etc. The six loans in this case were all ordinary loans, with loan dates of May 18, 1992, June 17, 1992, August 18, 1992, October 20, 1992, February 26, 1993, and November 18, 1993, with loan terms of twelve months and six months respectively, and purposes including funds for the Huaye Villa project (which is unrelated to the cooperative project), land purchase, working capital, etc., totaling RMB 44 million. These loans differ from the loans required for the Huashan New Village Project and the Shishan Resort Project as described in the cooperation agreements, proving that these loans are not loans under the cooperation agreements. 2. The finding of the first-instance judgment that the Qujiang Sub-branch of China Construction Bank used RMB 11 million from the ordinary loans to subscribe for legal person shares of Huashan Joint Stock Company is inconsistent with the facts. When Huashan Joint Stock Company was established in 1994, Shaanxi Construction Trust subscribed for 11 million legal person shares and additionally paid RMB 12 million (including RMB 1 million as handling fees) to Huashan Company for this purpose. This sum has no connection whatsoever with the ordinary loans mentioned above. The basis for the first instance's finding that the RMB 11 million was related to the ordinary loans was a photocopy of the "Basic Information of Hainan Huashan Industrial Co., Ltd." dated May 30, 1997, from the Second Sub-branch of China Construction Bank. The Qujiang Sub-branch of China Construction Bank does not acknowledge this. The court of first instance's reliance on this as a basis for finding facts violates the rules of evidence in litigation. 3. The first-instance judgment conflated two independent legal relationships: the cooperative relationship and the loan relationship. The first-instance judgment mixed the loan relationship with the cooperative relationship, which is inconsistent with the facts. Xinda Xi'an Office has never denied the existence of a cooperative relationship between the parties. The reason Xinda Xi'an Office filed the lawsuit for the loan is that the loan has nothing to do with the cooperative relationship; the two are independent of each other. The debt claimed in this case is not a debt under the cooperation agreement but a separate debt of Huashan Company, which cannot be borne jointly by both parties. In summary, the first-instance judgment erred in fact-finding and improperly applied the law. Xinda Xi'an Office requests that the court of second instance reverse the first-instance judgment, amend the judgment to order Huashan Company to repay the loan principal and interest, and bear all litigation costs of this case.

In response to the appeal requests and grounds of Xinda Xi'an Office, Huashan Company argued: 1. The appeal ground of Xinda Xi'an Office that "the first-instance judgment erred in fact-finding" cannot stand. (a) Although some loan contracts were entered into earlier in time than the cooperation contracts, under the circumstances where real estate development in Hainan was not standardized at that time, the true purpose of the loans was determined not by time, but by the true intent of the parties to the loan contracts. The actual use of the loan proceeds was to fulfill the loans stipulated in the cooperation contracts. The 1995 Loan Contract No. 010, submitted as evidence by Xinda Xi'an Office in the first instance, proves: the original loan of RMB 34 million, together with the unpaid interest on that loan of RMB 34 million converted into principal of RMB 10 million, resulted in a total loan principal of RMB 44 million. In the 1998 Loan Contract No. 98026, it was explicitly stipulated: a loan of RMB 44 million to repay the original loan of RMB 44 million (the original loan was used for the Shishan development). Through these two contracts, Huashan Company and the Qujiang Sub-branch of China Construction Bank have confirmed that the loans under the originally signed contracts had all been treated as project loans under the cooperation contracts. (b) Regarding the issue of the RMB 11 million share payment. Evidence such as the "Basic Information of Hainan Huashan Industrial Co., Ltd.," the "Letter of Authorization," and the "Explanation of Capital Verification Matters" attached to the "Capital Verification Report" issued by the Qujiang Sub-branch of China Construction Bank proves: Shaanxi Construction Trust had authorized Huashan Company to convert RMB 11 million from the cooperative project loans it provided to Huashan Company into its capital contribution for purchasing shares in Huashan Joint Stock Company. Whether Shaanxi Construction Trust contributed capital in the form of land valuation or cash, it was all funds from the cooperative loans or assets formed from land purchased with those loans. 2. The appeal ground of Xinda Xi'an Office that "the first-instance judgment improperly applied the law" cannot stand. The first-instance judgment did not confuse the cooperative relationship with the loan relationship; it is Xinda Xi'an Office that confuses the two. In summary, the appeal requests of Xinda Xi'an Office lack factual and legal basis. Huashan Company requests that the Supreme People's Court dismiss the appeal and affirm the original judgment.

The third party, the Qujiang Sub-branch of China Construction Bank, stated that it agreed with the appeal opinion of Xinda Xi'an Office.

This Court does not accept the fact found by the court of first instance that "Shaanxi Construction Trust subscribed for 11 million shares of Huashan Joint Stock Company." Additionally, during the second instance of this case, the "Debt Amount Verification Sheet" issued by the Second Sub-branch of China Construction Bank to Huashan Company on November 5, 1999, was subject to cross-examination. Xinda Xi'an Office provided a photocopy of evidence containing the handwritten content: "The above attachments are causally linked to the Debt Amount Verification Sheet, have inseparable characteristics, and have the same legal effect." Huashan Company provided an original piece of evidence containing the same content in printed text. The Qujiang Sub-branch of China Construction Bank provided an original piece of evidence without the above content. Given that the relevant evidence provided by the parties is inconsistent, this Court does not determine whether the "Debt Amount Verification Sheet" contained the above content. The other facts found in the first-instance judgment are affirmed.

This Court holds that the parties in this case all acknowledge the existence of facts concerning the cooperation contracts and loan contracts between them. The main focus of the dispute is whether the loan contracts under which Xinda Xi'an Office claims repayment of principal and interest from Huashan Company are related to the cooperation contracts signed between Huashan Company and the Qujiang Sub-branch of China Construction Bank.

Based on the previously signed "Economic Cooperation Contract," Huashan Company and Shaanxi Construction Trust also signed contracts such as the "Contract for Cooperative Construction of the 'Shishan Resort' Project." The aforementioned contracts all indicate that the parties had a clearly divided cooperative relationship in real estate development projects such as Shishan Resort, with Huashan Company specifically responsible for real estate development work and Shaanxi Construction Trust responsible for the necessary fundraising for the real estate development. The parties made clear stipulations regarding the source and order of repayment of funds borrowed by Huashan Company from Shaanxi Construction Trust in Huashan Company's name, reflecting the cooperative principle of sharing profits and bearing risks. Xinda Xi'an Office claims that the loan contracts in this case have no connection with the cooperation contracts and constitute two independent legal relationships. However, the Loan Contract No. 98026, signed between Huashan Company and the Qujiang Sub-branch of China Construction Bank, which is an important piece of evidence submitted by Xinda Xi'an Office in its lawsuit demanding repayment from Huashan Company, explicitly records: "The original loan was used for the Shishan development." This contract represents the consolidation and rollover of the original RMB 44 million loans involved in this case, proving that the Qujiang Sub-branch of China Construction Bank clearly recognized that the loans it issued to Huashan Company in this case were indeed used for the development project specified in the cooperation contract signed by both parties. During the process of the Qujiang Sub-branch of China Construction Bank transferring the creditor's rights to Xinda Xi'an Office and demanding payment, Huashan Company repeatedly and clearly stated that the relationship between the parties was a cooperative contractual relationship, and Xinda Xi'an Office and the Qujiang Sub-branch of China Construction Bank raised no objection to this before the lawsuit. The above evidence demonstrates a close connection between the loan contracts in this case and the cooperation contracts. The appeal claim of Xinda Xi'an Office that the loan contracts in this case are unrelated to the cooperation contracts cannot stand.

Xinda Xi'an Office argues that most of the loan contracts in this case were signed before the cooperation contracts, denying any connection between the two based on the chronological order. The motives, purposes, and functions of parties entering into civil contracts are complex. A contract can play a normative and guiding role, meaning parties regulate and guide future rights and obligations through offer and acceptance. A contract can also play a role of confirmation and evaluation, meaning parties use the contract to evaluate, confirm, supplement, and perfect the nature, purpose, and function of prior civil juristic acts. In this case, the parties, through civil juristic acts such as signing the cooperation contracts and the rollover loan contract, confirmed the nature, content, and function of the earlier loan contracts. Xinda Xi'an Office's denial of the connection between the loan contracts and the cooperation contracts based solely on the chronological order of signing lacks factual and legal basis. During the litigation, Xinda Xi'an Office also provided evidence materials showing other loans between the Qujiang Sub-branch of China Construction Bank and Huashan Company, claiming that these loans were under the cooperation contracts, thereby excluding the possibility that the loans in this case were under the cooperation contracts. However, these evidence materials are mostly internal bank accounting vouchers, whose authenticity is not acknowledged by Huashan Company. Xinda Xi'an Office failed to provide relevant evidence such as loan contracts to prove its claim; the above evidence cannot prove that these funds were loans related to the cooperation contracts. Moreover, even if Xinda Xi'an Office could prove that these loans were under the cooperation contracts, it does not directly lead to the conclusion that the loans in this case are not under the cooperation contracts; the above loans can coexist under the cooperation contracts without necessarily being mutually exclusive. The parties' burden of proof and cross-examination should focus on the key issue of whether the loans in this case are related to the cooperation contracts. In this litigation, Xinda Xi'an Office failed to provide evidence proving that the loans under the loan contracts in this case are other loans independent of the cooperation contracts. Its litigation claim that Huashan Company should repay the loan according to the loan contract terms without being affected by the cooperation contract cannot stand.

Xinda Xi'an Office's claim, based on the loan contracts, demanding that Huashan Company repay the loan lacks factual and legal basis, and its litigation request cannot stand. Under these circumstances, whether or not the source of funds for the 11 million shares of Huashan Joint Stock Company subscribed by Shaanxi Construction Trust is clarified, it will not affect the final outcome of this case. However, the determination of the above facts may affect the determination of other civil legal relationships between the parties. It was improper for the court of first instance to determine this disputed part of the facts in the civil judgment of this case, and this Court does not affirm it.

Xinda Xi'an Office is the transferee of the transferred creditor's rights, not a party to the cooperation contracts. In this litigation, it only asserted the legal relationship of the loan contract and did not put forward any litigation requests concerning the cooperation contracts. The Qujiang Sub-branch of China Construction Bank and Huashan Company are parties to the cooperation contracts, and neither party raised any litigation requests concerning the cooperation contracts in this loan dispute lawsuit. A people's court cannot render a judgment beyond the scope of the parties' litigation requests. Issues concerning the civil liability of the relevant parties arising from the signing and performance of the creditor's rights transfer contract and the cooperation contract may be resolved in separate actions.

In this case, the signing and performance of the loan contracts are part of the content of performing the cooperation contracts. According to the content agreed upon in the cooperation contracts, the parties were to share risks and profits for the cooperative project, and the parties made clear stipulations in the cooperation contracts regarding the order of fund allocation. Xinda Xi'an Office now separates the loan contracts from the cooperation contracts and independently requests Huashan Company to bear the loan principal and interest, which has no factual basis. The first-instance judgment's dismissal of Xinda Xi'an Office's litigation request was not erroneous, and this Court affirms it.

In summary, the facts found by the first-instance judgment are basically clear, and the application of law is correct. Pursuant to Article 153, paragraph 1, item (1) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, this Court hereby renders the following judgment:

The appeal is dismissed, and the original judgment is affirmed.

The second-instance acceptance fee of this case is RMB 176,540.25, to be borne by the Xi'an Office of China Xinda Asset Management Corporation.

This judgment is final.

Presiding Judge: Qian Xiaochen
Acting Judge: Liu Min
Acting Judge: Yang Zhengyu

January 5, 2009

Clerk: Yuan Hongxia

[Profile of the Presiding Judge]

Qian Xiaochen, Senior Judge: Born in 1968, Doctor of Laws, appointed as a judge of the Supreme People's Court in 2006.
